messages:
maya: Heads up — invoice INV-2025-0123 for ClearHealth shows a $12,300 burst/overage line tied to Dedicated commit tkn-6b4f. Customer says they had reserved 12k units; can we reconcile? cc @oliver @li
oliver: I'm on it. Which date range? Any SLA credits applied already?
maya: Jan 1–31, 2025. No credits on invoice. They flagged it after finance sent final invoice.
billing-bot: Invoice INV-2025-0123 | customer: ClearHealth | total: $72,450 | burst_overage: $12,300 | period: 2025-01-01 — 2025-01-31 | commits: dedicated_commit_id=tkn-6b4f | status: finalized
li: Re-running usage query now. If anyone needs the raw rows I can paste. Query: ```SELECT date, commit_id, tokens_used, commit_units_allocated FROM billing.usage WHERE customer='clearhealth' AND period='2025-01';```
li: Returned rows show a sustained spike 01-12 — 01-14 with tokens ~3.2M/day vs typical 280k/day. Looks like customer hit burst cap and we charged overage.
arjun: Did their Dedicated plan include burst allowance? Pricing sheet says reserved 12,000 units/month + 25% burst at on-demand rate. Need to check pricing experiment promo code `FEB_PILOT_10` — might apply 10% off bursts.
li: Promo not listed on the account. But I see a one-off discount code 'pilot-jan' attached, applies to hosted API only, not Dedicated. So no discount.
oliver: For SLA credit calc: SLA target was 99.5% with 12 minutes downtime on 01-13 (incident INC-2025-0021). Finance, do we net credits against burst charges or issue separate line item?
maya: Customer expects a gross credit line, not netting. They prefer clear invoice adjustments.
arjun: Based on SLA rules, uptime shortfall triggers 10% monthly credit on committed fee (~$4,200). That doesn't cover burst charges. We should issue two items: SLA credit (invoice adj) and a usage reconciliation that refunds mistaken overage if our system mis-attributed commit capacity.
li: I confirmed the spike occurred during a failover period; routing policy temporarily sent traffic to on-demand pool for ~36 hours due to autoscale cold-starts. That legitimately generated on-demand tokens, so charge stands. But we should share detailed breakdown and timestamped logs with the customer.
oliver: Proposed resolution: (1) Provide detailed per-day token table + logs; (2) Apply SLA credit $4,200; (3) Offer one-time courtesy 25% discount on the burst portion ($3,075) as goodwill. Need managerial sign-off from @maya.
maya: Approved. Apply the SLA credit and the 25% courtesy on the burst line. Also add a short explanation email and attach the logs. Finance, please generate credit memo and adjusted invoice INV-2025-0123R. :thumbsup:
billing-bot: Credit memo created CM-2025-0009 | SLA_credit: $4,200 | Goodwill_discount_on_burst: $3,075 | Adjusted_total: $65,175
oliver: Noted. Action items: @li prepare daily token CSV and attach S3 link; @arjun draft the email to ClearHealth; @maya confirm wording. I'll route the CM for posting.
li: Uploaded CSV to s3://redwood-invoices/clearhealth/INV-2025-0123/breakdown.csv — sharing link: https://s3.redwood.com/clearhealth/INV-2025-0123/breakdown.csv
arjun: Draft sent to @maya for review: 'Hi ClearHealth — we investigated the January spike, attached breakdown and logs, applied SLA credit and a one-time courtesy discount on burst charges. Please let us know if you'd like a call to review.'
maya: Looks good. Send it and cc billing@redwood.com. Please flag if customer pushes for full refund.
oliver: Done. CM posted and adjusted invoice emailed. Closing thread unless customer escalates.
